name: Meditron 7B
usecase: Medical exam prep and clinical Q&A. Fine-tuned on medical guidelines, textbooks, and clinical practice papers from PubMed.
strength: USMLE-style questions, clinical decision support, drug-disease reasoning.

name: Meditron 70B
usecase: High-accuracy clinical reasoning at scale. Best open model for complex multi-step medical problem solving.
strength: State-of-the-art on MedQA and PubMedQA among open models. Ideal for research pipelines.

name: BioMistral 7B
usecase: Biomedical text understanding and generation. Pre-trained on PubMed Central full-text articles.
strength: Strong on biomedical NER, relation extraction, and research paper QA.

name: OpenBioLLM 70B
usecase: Top-performing open medical LLM. Outperforms GPT-4 on several medical benchmarks. Ideal for clinical NLP pipelines.
strength: Best-in-class open model for USMLE, MedQA, PubMedQA. Strong instruction following for clinical tasks.

name: OpenBioLLM 8B
usecase: Lightweight medical LLM for edge deployment. Great balance of performance and resource requirements.
strength: Runs on consumer hardware. Solid performance on medical QA tasks.

name: Med42 70B
usecase: Clinical AI assistant fine-tuned by healthcare professionals. Designed with patient safety guardrails.
strength: Medically verified responses, strong on clinical vignettes, drug interactions, and triage.

name: MedAlpaca 13B
usecase: Medical instruction following for QA and patient-facing applications. Trained on Alpaca-style medical dialogues.
strength: Conversational medical QA, patient education, symptom explanation.

name: PMC-LLaMA 13B
usecase: Biomedical literature understanding. Fine-tuned on 4.8M PubMed abstracts and 100k+ PubMed Central papers.
strength: Research paper QA, evidence synthesis, biomedical fact extraction from literature.

name: ClinicalCamel 30B
usecase: Clinical note generation and EHR-style text processing. Trained on USMLE and clinical dialogue datasets.
strength: Clinical documentation, discharge summaries, clinical reasoning from patient histories.

name: BioGPT
usecase: Biomedical text generation and question answering. Pre-trained on 15M PubMed abstracts.
strength: Relation extraction, biomedical NER, PubMed-grounded QA. Lightweight and fast.

name: BioBERT Large
usecase: The workhorse of biomedical NLP. Best for named entity recognition, relation extraction, and biomedical text classification.
strength: Disease NER, drug-drug interaction detection, biomedical text classification pipelines.

name: ClinicalBERT
usecase: Clinical note understanding. Trained on MIMIC-III discharge summaries. Best for EHR-derived NLP tasks.
strength: Clinical NER from free-text notes, ICD coding assistance, clinical text classification.

name: PubMedBERT
usecase: Pre-trained from scratch on PubMed. Superior to general BERT for biomedical downstream tasks.
strength: Biomedical NLI, NER, text classification, and sentence embeddings for retrieval.

name: GatorTron 3.9B
usecase: Large clinical language model trained on 90B words of de-identified clinical text from UF Health.
strength: Clinical concept extraction, medical NLI, clinical text classification from real EHR data.

name: SciBERT
usecase: Scientific text understanding. Trained on 1.14M scientific papers from Semantic Scholar. Good baseline for health research NLP.
strength: Scientific NER, citation classification, research paper classification.

name: BlueBERT
usecase: Joint biomedical and clinical NLP. Trained on both PubMed and MIMIC-III.
strength: NER tasks bridging research literature and clinical notes. Good for cross-domain health NLP.

name: LLaMA 3.1 8B
usecase: Strong general-purpose base for health RAG pipelines. Excellent instruction following makes it easy to prompt for structured clinical output.
strength: Health RAG, structured JSON output, clinical report summarization.

name: Mistral 7B
usecase: Efficient general model widely used as a base for medical fine-tuning. Great for health RAG with structured retrieval.
strength: Fast inference, solid reasoning, good JSON compliance for structured health data output.

name: Gemma 2 9B
usecase: High-quality reasoning in a mid-size model. Performs well above its weight class on medical QA benchmarks.
strength: Clinical reasoning, health claim verification, evidence appraisal.

name: Qwen 2.5 7B
usecase: Excellent structured output reliability. Great for health RAG pipelines that require consistent JSON responses.
strength: JSON reliability, multilingual health content, structured data extraction.

name: Phi-3.5 Mini
usecase: Best small model for health use cases. Runs on edge devices and mobile. Surprisingly strong on medical reasoning for its size.
strength: On-device health apps, offline triage tools, low-latency clinical chatbots.
